The claim states that the output is a final composited image with correct volumetric shadows, citing Source [S1]. Since all aspects of the claim (final composited image, correct volumetric shadows) are directly supported by the text in Source [S1], the verdict is supported.

The strength $P_{i,j+k}$ of a ray as it leaves a sample location is computed from the strength $P_{i,j}$ as it approaches the sample and the opacity $\alpha$ of the sample [S1]:

The claim states that the strength $P_{i,j+k}$ is computed from the strength $P_{i,j}$ and the opacity $ eta$ of the sample. However, the evidence (Source [S1]) provides the formula $P_{i,j+k} = P_{i,j} (1 -  rac{k_{i,j}}{d^2})$. In this formula, the variables are $P_{i,j}$ (strength approaching), $k_{i,j}$ (a constant), and $d$ (distance from the light source). The opacity $ eta$ is mentioned in the text as being computed to attenuate the ray strength, but it is not a variable in the specific mathematical formula provided for calculating $P_{i,j+k}$ in the evidence. The formula relies on distance and a constant, not explicitly on the opacity value in the equation shown.

All specific claims in the statement are directly supported by the text in Source [S1].
